subject: Second native Chalk pass following the palette and surface feedback
reader: Parker, who reviewed the first build and supplied screenshots of the missing surfaces

sections.heading: Chalk · second native pass
sections.text:
This build applies your Chalk feedback to Terminal Delight. Choose the colours through your usual theme, then choose Chalk under Skin for paper surfaces, larger handwriting and chalk selection strokes. There is one Chalk choice. The captures below show the running native app.

sections.heading: Follow the chosen palette
sections.text:
The first build gave Chalk its own colours. Your review corrected that boundary: Chalk is the surface, and the active theme supplies the colours. These two native windows select the same Chalk skin, first with your Praus palette and saved display settings, then with Flexoki Light. Once that boundary is in place, the remaining work is to carry the material through every control. 01 · Praus · your current theme 
Praus keeps its charcoal, sage and linen; the cabinet, pane rims and controls now wear the paper material. 02 · Flexoki Light · the same Chalk skin 
Switching the palette produces pale stock without choosing another Chalk design. The terminal keeps its monospace font.

sections.heading: Complete the surrounding controls
sections.text:
Changing the colour boundary did not cover the gaps in your screenshots. The menus, gauges, attention spine and outer frame each had rendering paths that bypassed the paper. They now use the shared stock and larger handwriting. These close-ups show the result; click one to inspect its full native window. 03 · Palette and rules 
The menu has one Chalk choice, larger handwriting, paper switches and a broad chalk swipe under selected captions. The same treatment reaches program-colour and syntax controls. 04 · Gauges on pale stock 
Tracks and thumbs use paper and chalk. Percentage readouts stay on one line; darker pigment keeps the marks visible on the light palette. 05 · Attention queue and spine 
The queue and its answer buttons share the stock. Larger text has room for the key hints, and a long queue scrolls inside the window. The cases in this capture are fictional. 06 · Paint cards 
The paint cards also use Chalk. Wider tiles fit palette names, and their selection swipe matches the other controls.

sections.heading: Carry the paper through the terminal
sections.text:
With the surrounding controls covered, your last screenshot finding remains: the terminal itself had not changed. Its paper must sit inside the same region as the text for CRT warp to carry both. Stock now paints there before the text grid, while a paper rim replaces the old raised bezel. The terminal keeps its current font and programme colours. 07 · Praus · CRT warp enabled 
The terminal stock bends with the terminal, while the header and cabinet remain their own surfaces. The sticky note retains its tape, fibres, flower and inverse warp.

sections.heading: Start the next pass from this review
sections.text:
That completes the surfaces named in this review. The native checks also caught clipped panels, wrapped percentages, overflowing paint names and visible texture joins; each correction is recorded with your ten screenshots. Those failures establish what the next pass must photograph again. The two choices below are ready for your next annotations. 

 Handwriting size 
Current choice: a 16 px optical floor before menu scaling, with wider tiles and earlier header overflow. 
 Chalk selection 
Current choice: an irregular pigment swipe behind the caption, with a dry chalk edge. 

Annotate a capture or either choice with what should change next. The next pass can start from those anchors and the saved record. 

 | 
 | Your review | This pass 
 | “CHALK --- is the surface” | One Chalk skin follows the active palette; the old Paper selection remains compatible. 
 | “the font is awkwardly small” | Optical sizing for handwriting; room reserved in tiles, readouts and pane headers. 
 | “needs to be the chalk stroke” | A textured swipe replaces the short selection bar. 
 | “theem surface was INCOMPLETE” | Cabinet, bands, pane rims, menus, spine/queue, gauges and paint cards now share stock. 
 | “The terminals themselves are unchanged” | Stock paints under the terminal grid inside its warp region. 
 | “TRACK THE STEPS ... AND THE FEEDBACK” | Versioned screenshots, step log, source hashes, native recipe and validation receipts. Verification, source and repeatable capture 
All scenes used a 1576 × 950 logical window on the 1.6× display. The PNGs are 2522 × 1520 pixels. WebP storage is lossless; decoded pixels were compared with the native PNGs. Terminal output and queue cases are staged examples. 

 | Rio core | 2,494 passed; 9 ignored

 | Strict Clippy, formatting and release | Passed 
 | Material selection and restart | Chosen through ctl, saved as Chalk, restored without a skin file 
 | Skin switching | Chalk → Default → Chalk in the same native window 08 · The existing Default skin 
Default keeps its existing typography and chrome. This is the same Flexoki Light scene after changing only the skin. 
The launcher is installed for the next GUI launch. The current window stays on its existing build; reopen TD and choose Skin → Chalk . The previous GUI-placement follow-up remains recorded. 
The renderer lives in paper.rs ; the material and typography live in skin.rs . The complete feedback and steps are in feedback and step record . Images, logs, source hashes and capture.sh are in reports/2026-10-19-chalk-surface-v02-evidence/ . Both the review images and the step record are retained for the next pass.
